passages.text: To seek God within ourselves avails us far more than to look for Him amongst creatures; Saint Augustine tells us how he found the Almighty within his own soul, after having long sought for Him elsewhere.
passages.note: Searching outside for what lies within

passages.text: We should make our petitions like beggars before a powerful and rich Emperor; then, with downcast eyes, humbly wait.
We should rather abandon our souls into the hands of God, leaving Him to do as He chooses with us, as far as possible forgetting all self-interest and resigning ourselves entirely to His will.

God gave us faculties for our use; each of them will receive its proper reward. Then do not let us try to charm them to sleep, but permit them to do their work until divinely called to something higher.
passages.note: Meditation without forcing the mind blank
